message.reasoning:
We are given a software specification and user stories. We need to estimate the development effort for the described software increment.

First, we break down the development into activities. The specification is about Spring XD on Cloud Foundry (CF) and involves implementing an Admin SPI (Service Provider Interface) for two different implementations: one for Receptor and one for Cloud Controller. It also involves creating a module registry abstraction, making the SPI profile-aware, integrating with Eureka for self-registration, and adding search capabilities by name and storing metadata in Eureka.

We note that the specification is a bit abstract, but we can infer the following activities:

1. Design the Admin SPI and the module registry abstraction.
2. Implement the Receptor implementation of the Admin SPI.
3. Implement the Cloud Controller implementation of the Admin SPI.
4. Create a common repository (common repo) for SPI implementations (as per U3).
5. Make the SPI implementation profile-aware so that the correct implementation is wired based on the deployment (e.g., java -jar, cf push, ltc create) (U5).
6. Implement self-registration of modules with Eureka when they are installed (U6).
7. Implement search by module name (aside from spring.application.name) (U7).
8. Implement storing module metadata in Eureka (U8).
9. Write unit tests and integration tests for each component.
10. Set up the build and configuration for the new modules and common repo.

We also note that the specification requires Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.0. We assume we are working in a Java17+ environment.

Now, we state the main technical and design decisions and assumptions:

Technical and Design Decisions:
- We will design the Admin SPI as a Java interface with the specified methods.
- We will use Spring profiles to conditionally wire the appropriate implementation (Receptor or Cloud Controller) based on the deployment environment.
- We will use Spring Boot's auto-configuration to wire the correct implementation.
- We will use Eureka client for self-registration and metadata storage.
- We will extend the module registry to support the new SPI and Eureka integration.
- We will use a common repository for the SPI interfaces and shared abstractions, separate from the implementation modules.

Assumptions:
- The development team is familiar with Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, and Eureka.
- We are starting from an existing Spring XD codebase and are adding new modules or modifying existing ones.
- We have access to the necessary Eureka server and Cloud Foundry environment for testing.
- The existing Spring XD Admin already has some infrastructure that we can build upon.
- We assume that the Receptor and Cloud Controller implementations require communication with external services (Receptor and Cloud Controller) and we need to handle that via REST clients or SDKs. We assume we have the necessary documentation or APIs for these services.
- We assume that the modules that need to self-register are Spring Boot applications and can include the necessary Eureka client dependency.

Now, we break down the activities and estimate the effort for each. We estimate in work-hours.

Activity 1: Design the Admin SPI and module registry abstraction.
- Define the interface and abstract classes for the Admin SPI.
- Design the module registry abstraction to support the SPI and future extensions.
- Effort: 16 hours.

Activity 2: Implement the Receptor implementation of the Admin SPI.
- Implement the interface methods (getStatus, listModules, and the map of module keys to status) using the Receptor client.
- Effort: 24 hours.

Activity 3: Implement the Cloud Controller implementation of the Admin SPI.
- Implement the interface methods using the Cloud Controller client.
- Effort: 24 hours.

Activity 4: Create a common repository for SPI implementations.
- Set up a new Maven/Gradle project (or module) for the common repo.
- Move the SPI interfaces and shared abstractions to this repo.
- Effort: 8 hours.

Activity 5: Make the SPI implementation profile-aware.
- Use Spring profiles and auto-configuration to conditionally load the appropriate implementation based on the deployment method (java -jar, cf push, ltc create).
- Effort: 16 hours.

Activity 6: Implement self-registration of modules with Eureka.
- Add Eureka client dependency to the modules.
- Implement the registration logic so that when a module is installed, it registers itself with Eureka.
- Effort: 16 hours.

Activity 7: Implement search by module name.
- Extend the module registry or create a new service to allow searching by module name (in addition to the default spring.application.name).
- Effort: 12 hours.

Activity 8: Implement storing module metadata in Eureka.
- Store additional module metadata (as per the requirement) in Eureka, possibly using instance metadata.
- Effort: 12 hours.

Activity 9: Write unit tests and integration tests.
- Write unit tests for each component (SPI implementations, registry, Eureka integration, etc.).
- Write integration tests that run in the target environment (if possible) or use embedded Eureka for testing.
- Effort: 40 hours.

Activity 10: Build and configuration setup.
- Set up the build for the new modules (if any) and the common repo.
- Configure the project structure and dependencies.
- Effort: 8 hours.

Now, we calculate the total effort:

Total = 16 + 24 + 24 + 8 + 16 + 16 + 12 + 12 + 40 + 8 = 176 hours.

We note that these are estimates for one developer. The specification says we are the developer responsible for all work, so we are estimating our own effort.

Now, we format the response as per the required JSON schema.

technical_and_design_decisions: Admin SPI will be defined as a Java interface with methods: getStatus(ModuleDescriptor), listModules(), and getModuleStatusMap() returning Map<ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus>.
Two implementations of Admin SPI: one using Receptor client API and one using Cloud Controller REST client.
Module registry abstraction will be a new Spring-based service layer providing SPI discovery and lifecycle management.

Profile-aware wiring will use Spring profiles with @ConditionalOnProperty or similar mechanism to auto-configure the correct Admin SPI implementation based on deployment method (java -jar, cf push, ltc create).
Eureka integration will use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka for service registration and metadata storage.
Modules will self-register with Eureka using a Spring Boot starter triggered during installation/startup.
Module search by name will extend Eureka's instance metadata with custom attributes and implement a query service.
Assume the existing Spring XD codebase is compatible with Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.0, and we can modify or add modules as needed.
assumptions: Development environment has Java 17+, Maven/Gradle, and access to required repositories.
The existing Spring XD infrastructure includes basic module deployment and administration, which we will extend.
Receptor and Cloud Controller client libraries or APIs are available and documented.
Eureka server is available for testing (or can be embedded for unit tests).
All modules (admin, receptors, cloud controller integration) are Spring Boot applications.
The scope includes implementation, unit tests, and basic integration tests, but not performance tuning or extensive security hardening.
The developer (myself) is familiar with Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, and the existing Spring XD codebase.

activities.activity_name: Design Admin SPI and module registry abstraction
activities.activity_description: Define the Admin SPI interface, ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus, and the module registry abstraction classes. Document the contracts and dependencies.
Implement the Admin SPI using the Receptor client API to query module status and health metrics, and integrate with the module registry.
Implement the Admin SPI using the Cloud Controller REST client to query module status and health metrics, and integrate with the module registry.

activities.activity_name: Create common repository for SPI implementations
activities.activity_description: Set up a dedicated repository or module for the Admin SPI interfaces, shared abstractions, and possibly common utilities. Configure build and documentation.
Use Spring profiles and auto-configuration to conditionally load the correct Admin SPI implementation (Receptor or Cloud Controller) based on the deployment method.
Add Eureka client dependencies and implement logic so modules self-register with Eureka upon installation, including initial metadata.
Extend the module registry or Eureka integration to allow searching for modules by a custom name attribute, in addition to the default spring.application.name.

activities.activity_name: Implement module metadata storage in Eureka
activities.activity_description: Store additional module metadata (status, health, etc.) in Eureka instance metadata, and ensure it is updated as module state changes.

activities.activity_name: Write unit tests for all new components
activities.activity_description: Write unit tests for Admin SPI implementations, module registry, profile-aware configuration, Eureka integration logic, and search functionality.
Write integration tests for end-to-end flows: module deployment, self-registration, Admin SPI queries, and metadata storage, using embedded or mocked Eureka and Cloud Foundry environment.
Set up Maven/Gradle build scripts, dependencies, and module structure for the new and modified modules, ensuring compatibility with Java 17+ and Spring Boot 3.0+.
